Coverage distinguishes the unnamed-service attribution from specific GRU campaigns and provides exposure, stream-access, network-segmentation, field-of-view, evidence-preservation, and incident-response guidance.

item.title: Hugging Face autonomous-agent production intrusion
item.description: Added Hugging Face's first-party disclosure of a production intrusion initiated through malicious-dataset processing. A remote-code loader and dataset-configuration template injection led from worker execution to node access, cloud and cluster credential harvesting, and lateral movement across internal clusters. The vendor attributes more than 17,000 logged actions to an autonomous agent framework but did not name the framework, model, actor, CVEs, or IOCs. Coverage distinguishes confirmed internal dataset and credential access from the vendor's finding of no public model, dataset, Space, container-image, or package tampering, and provides dataset-sandboxing, workload-identity, egress, telemetry, token-response, and forensic guidance.

item.title: NGINX CVE-2026-42533 two-pass capture-clobbering RCE risk
item.description: Added NGINX, F5, and researcher coverage of CVE-2026-42533, a configuration-dependent heap overflow caused by regex map evaluation clobbering capture state between NGINX script-engine sizing and writing passes. The page captures the 15-year affected range, fixed 1.30.4 and 1.31.3 builds, worker-crash and RCE risk, the researcher's ASLR-bypass memory-disclosure claim, vulnerable directive patterns, temporary named-capture mitigation, and an explicit caveat that no confirmed exploitation of this CVE was identified.

item.title: SleeperGem RubyGems maintainer-account compromise
item.description: Added Aikido Security and StepSecurity coverage of SleeperGem, a coordinated RubyGems supply-chain attack targeting developer workstations through malicious git_credential_manager, Dendreo, and fastlane-plugin-run_tests_firebase_testlab releases. The page captures dormant maintainer-account compromise, CI-environment evasion, require-time execution, Forgejo payload staging, systemd and cron persistence, the setuid-shell privilege path, registry hashes, host artifacts, and credential-rotation guidance.

item.title: HelloNet ViPNet update-system campaign
item.description: Added Kaspersky coverage of an active targeted campaign that persists by sideloading wtsapi32.dll through the startup-launched ViPNet update component. The page captures HelloInjector process injection, HelloProxy protocol markers, HelloExecutor and HelloCleaner follow-ons, the Rust HelloBackdoor, reverse SSH tunneling, targeted Russian sectors, and the low-confidence Chinese-speaking attribution caveat.

item.title: GoSerpent Southeast Asia espionage campaign
item.description: Added Kaspersky GReAT coverage of a government and diplomatic espionage operation using GoSerpent, McMx, ThumbcacheService, Stowaway, and TmcLoader/TmcPayload. The page captures delayed document collection, credential dumping, chained proxying, network-share exfiltration, durable file and infrastructure pivots, and the uncertain TetrisPhantom relationship.

item.title: NadMesh AI-service and cloud-credential botnet
item.description: Added QiAnXin XLab coverage of NadMesh, an autonomous Go botnet that prioritizes exposed ComfyUI, Ollama, n8n, Open WebUI, Langflow, Gradio, and MCP services while also exploiting Docker, Kubernetes, Redis, Jenkins, and weak remote-access credentials. The page captures AWS and Kubernetes credential theft, polymorphic builds, three-way SSH/agent/cron persistence, operator-panel scale caveats, high-priority ports, behavioral hunts, and revoke-before-recovery guidance.

item.title: ViteVenom / ChainVeil npm campaign
item.description: Added Checkmarx Zero coverage of seven malicious scoped npm packages impersonating Vite and Vitest tooling. ViteVenom uses import-time execution, mixed clean and malicious package versions, detached Node.js persistence, and Tron/Aptos/Binance Smart Chain payload resolution; shared Tier-2 wallets, XOR keys, and a final RAT link it with high confidence to SuccessKey's ChainVeil infrastructure.

item.title: ACR Stealer ClickFix campaigns: WebDAV/Python and MSHTA/steganography intrusion chains
item.description: Added Microsoft Threat Intelligence coverage of increased ACR Stealer activity from late April through mid-June 2026. The new page captures two observed ClickFix-led intrusion chains: WebDAV/rundll32/pushd delivery with bundled Python loaders, scheduled-task persistence, Fiber API in-memory execution, and EtherHiding-style blockchain C2 resolution; and an MSHTA/VBScript/PowerShell chain that extracts encrypted shellcode from JPEG pixels. Defender guidance focuses on ClickFix paste-and-run telemetry, remote WebDAV DLL loading, conhost --headless, mshta remote HTA execution, browser Login Data / Web Data access, DPAPI decryption, and document staging from OneDrive / SharePoint synced paths.

item.title: AsyncAPI Miasma: Microsoft pwn-request root-cause and Defender detection update
item.description: Updated AsyncAPI Miasma coverage with Microsoft Threat Intelligence's July 15 analysis: a pull_request_target pwn-request exposed the asyncapi-bot PAT, unauthorized commits reached auto-publish branches, and legitimate OIDC release workflows produced valid npm provenance under npm-oidc-no-reply@github[.]com. The update also captures the staged publish timeline, Yarn-cache observation, M-RED-TEAM v6.4 / miasma-train-p1 details, Defender detections Trojan:JS/MiasmStealer.SC and Trojan:Script/Supychain.A, and response guidance for cache purge, sync.js hunts, C2 blocking, and credential rotation after import-time execution.

item.title: OkoBot cryptocurrency-wallet malware framework
item.description: Added Kaspersky GReAT coverage of OkoBot, an active Windows malware framework that starts with TookPS, uses SSH-bot payload delivery, and includes SeedHunter process injection into Trezor Suite, Ledger Wallet, and Ledger Live to collect seed phrases from inside legitimate wallet applications. The page captures USB-gated prompting, moonsand[.]store C2, artifact exfiltration, affected-country telemetry, and wallet compromise response guidance.

item.title: KNX Protocol CVE-2023-4346 KEV exploitation
item.description: Added CISA KEV coverage for CVE-2023-4346 affecting KNX Protocol Connection Authorization Option 1. CISA says exploitation can purge devices without additional security options enabled and set a BCU key that locks the device, making this a building-automation and facility-control recovery risk with a July 29, 2026 due date.

item.title: Oracle E-Business Suite CVE-2026-46817: CISA KEV update
item.description: Updated Oracle E-Business Suite CVE-2026-46817 coverage after CISA added the Oracle Payments takeover flaw to KEV on July 15 with a July 18 remediation due date. Exposed EBS systems should be treated as forensics-triage candidates, not patch-only tickets.

item.title: Patriot Bait AI-assisted C2 botnet
item.description: Added Trend Micro / TrendAI coverage of Patriot Bait / bandcampro, a Russian-speaking actor observed using Gemini CLI as the primary operator interface for a small C2 botnet. The page captures the six-minute C2 migration, plain-text skill-file operating model, PowerShell polling agent, Cloudflare tunnel troubleshooting, API and persistence pivots, and behavioral guidance for disposable AI-regenerated infrastructure.

item.title: NuGet game-cheat DotnetTool pepesoft campaign
item.description: Added Socket coverage of 11 malicious NuGet DotnetTool packages posing as game cheats and panels. The packages run .NET downloaders that stage pepesoft.exe from pepegit666 GitHub Releases or Hugging Face paths, use DNS-over-HTTPS for GitHub resolution, request clock-resync elevation in most samples, and launch PyInstaller / PyArmor Python payloads with Google Sheets telemetry, hardware-ID binding, proxy fallback, and Telegram screenshot-control paths in direct-bytecode builds.

item.title: LabubaRAT Rust remote-access trojan
item.description: Added Blackpoint Cyber / The Hacker News coverage of LabubaRAT, a Rust-based Windows RAT masquerading as NVIDIA runtime software. The page captures runtime-supplied C2 configuration, local SQLite state, HTTPS / WebView2 / DNS-tunneling communications, security-tool and browser profiling, SOCKS5 proxying, command / PowerShell / JavaScript execution, screenshot capture, and NVIDIA-impersonation defender hunts.

item.title: AsyncAPI generator next-branch Miasma compromise
item.description: Added StepSecurity coverage of the July 14 AsyncAPI generator monorepo compromise: an attacker pushed to the next branch, triggered the legitimate release-with-changesets GitHub Actions workflow, and published malicious @asyncapi/generator, generator-helpers, generator-components, and specs versions with valid npm OIDC provenance. The page captures runtime require() execution, IPFS sync.js staging, Miasma v3 multi-channel RAT capabilities, C2 indicators, and trusted-publishing hardening guidance.

item.title: Injective SDK npm wallet stealer: JFrog runtime reachability and header-exfiltration update
item.description: Updated Injective SDK compromise coverage with JFrog's July 12 runtime analysis: PrivateKey.generate(), MsgBroadcasterWithPk, and CosmJS-compatible wallet wrappers can route mnemonics or raw/byte-array private keys through the infected PrivateKey class, and the stealer sends base64-encoded secrets in the X-Request-Id header of empty gRPC-Web-looking POSTs to an Injective-looking endpoint.

item.title: jscrambler npm compromise: follow-on malicious releases and runtime trigger shift
item.description: Updated jscrambler coverage with Socket and npm registry follow-up: after the initial 8.14.0 preinstall stealer, the actor pushed 8.16.0, 8.17.0, 8.18.0, and 8.20.0. Later releases moved the same native Rust infostealer payload from preinstall execution into runtime files, expanding hunts beyond lifecycle-script telemetry to dist/index.js and dist/bin/jscrambler.js diffs.

item.title: Joomla extension KEV exploitation cluster: Balbooa Forms / iCagenda update
item.description: Updated Joomla KEV coverage after CISA added Balbooa Forms CVE-2026-56291 and iCagenda CVE-2026-48939 on July 10, expanding the July 7 JoomShaper SP Page Builder and Joomlack Page Builder active-exploitation cluster. Treat exposed Joomla extension arbitrary-file-upload flaws as likely CMS web-shell risk until logs and file systems are reviewed.

item.title: Agent localhost control-plane RCE: OpenClaw WhatsApp-to-host update
item.description: Updated agent localhost control-plane guidance with OpenClaw GitHub Security Advisories and public WhatsApp-to-host reporting: patched host-execution filtering and sandbox bind-mount flaws could let lower-trust messaging, plugin, repository, or webhook input cross into command execution, credential access, or stronger authorization scopes. The page now captures GHSA-hjr6-g723-hmfm, GHSA-9969-8g9h-rxwm, GHSA-575v-8hfq-m3mc, OpenClaw 2026.6.6 upgrade guidance, and Gateway hardening controls.

item.title: O-UNC-066 Entra passkey vishing
item.description: Added Okta Threat Intelligence coverage of O-UNC-066 passkey-themed vishing against Microsoft Entra enrollment flows, including passkey-domain lures, victim-branded Microsoft 365 pages, live operator control, fake BIP-39 recovery-key distractions, attacker-controlled passkey registration risk, and defender guidance for authentication-method enrollment telemetry.

item.title: WP-SHELLSTORM webshell access brokerage
item.description: Added SOCRadar coverage of WP-SHELLSTORM, an exposed attacker infrastructure case showing 1.4M+ targeted domains, 27 weaponized CVEs, 5,700+ active webshells, Breeze Cache Cleaner / ThemeREX / Joomla JCE exploit productivity, parallel Nacos credential theft, and webshell access-broker defender guidance.

item.title: Operation Phnom Penh MODBEACON activity
item.description: Added Qianxin coverage of Operation Phnom Penh, where a Silver Fox / UTG-Q-1000 Ghost distributor used counterfeit-software SEO lures and Ghost infrastructure to deliver MODBEACON, a Rust-linked Windows implant using gRPC over HTTP/2, token authentication, host fingerprinting, WMI persistence, and in-memory plugins.

item.title: MODBEACON
item.description: Added MODBEACON as a Windows memory-resident stage / implant reported by Qianxin, with gRPC-over-HTTP/2 C2, Xray/V2Ray-inspired transport, agent-token authentication, host fingerprinting, native-v3 in-memory plugins, Ghost delivery infrastructure, and concrete C2 / hash indicators.

item.title: Braintree.Net NuGet payment skimmer
item.description: Added Socket coverage of the Braintree.Net NuGet typosquat, which copied PayPal Braintree's .NET SDK surface while intercepting production payment-card data, Braintree merchant credentials, and host environment secrets. The page captures affected Braintree.Net, DependencyInjector.Core, SipNet, and SipNet.OpenAI.Realtime versions, inflated placeholder-download reputation abuse, api.348672-shakepay[.]com exfiltration paths, and PCI-focused defender guidance.

item.title: Pakistani law enforcement espionage convergence
item.description: Added SentinelOne coverage of suspected China- and India-nexus espionage converging on Pakistani law enforcement from 2024 to 2026, including Balochistan Police targeting, PlugX / ShadowPad / Cobalt Strike / Remcos C2 windows, TAG-179 / Mysterious Elephant / APT-C-08 context, and cms_plugin.exe implants hosted from a police Complaint Management System portal.

item.title: Injective SDK npm wallet stealer
item.description: Added Socket coverage of the compromised @injectivelabs/sdk-ts@1.20.21 npm release, which hooked normal wallet key-derivation paths to exfiltrate mnemonics and private-key material through an Injective-looking endpoint. The page captures the 17 additional @injectivelabs packages pinned to the malicious SDK version, source-repository / maintainer-account compromise timeline, affected file hashes, transitive dependency risk, and defender guidance for lockfile hunts, cache eviction, clean upgrades, and wallet key rotation.

item.title: GodDamn ransomware PoisonX BYOVD activity
item.description: Added Broadcom / Symantec coverage of GodDamn ransomware, the latest Monster → Beast → GodDamn Hyadina rebrand, with PoisonX signed-driver defense evasion, AnyDesk and PsExec lateral movement, NirSoft / Mimikatz credential harvesting, g11.sys driver pivots, encryptor indicators, and defender guidance for signed-driver inventory, EDR tamper response, and ransomware credential rotation.

item.title: AI coding-agent symlink write confusion
item.description: Added Wiz GhostApproval and Adversa AI SymJack coverage for AI coding-assistant symlink write-confusion: malicious repositories can make agents approve or execute benign-looking workspace writes while the canonical path resolves to SSH, agent/MCP configuration, shell startup, CI, or other sensitive files outside the workspace. The page captures affected assistant status, CVE-2026-12958 and CVE-2026-50549, workspace-boundary lessons, and defender controls for canonical-path enforcement, symlink inventory, auto-approve restrictions, and credential rotation.

item.title: npm install explicit-trust controls: npm v12 GA / bypass2fa deprecation update
item.description: Updated npm install explicit-trust controls after GitHub announced npm v12 is generally available and tagged latest. The update records install scripts off by default, explicit Git and remote dependency allowance, and the deprecation path for granular access tokens with bypass2fa privileges, with defender guidance for project testing, approval inventory, package-manager configuration drift, and legacy publication-token cleanup.

item.title: REF6045 / SCMBANKER Mexican banking fraud
item.description: Added Elastic Security Labs coverage of REF6045 / SCMBANKER, a Mexico-focused operator-assisted banking-fraud operation using ClickFix fake-CAPTCHA pages to stage a PowerShell toolkit. The page captures Windows Run validation.txt delivery, bitsadmin / PowerShell staging, banking-session monitoring, screenshots, vishing overlays, browser redirects, clipboard account-number replacement, Remote Utilities escalation, exposed infrastructure pivots, and Elastic's LLM-assisted tooling-development caveat.

item.title: SCMBANKER
item.description: Added SCMBANKER as a PowerShell banking-fraud toolkit used by REF6045 against Mexican financial targets, with defender pivots for ClickFix-to-validation.txt execution, bitsadmin script retrieval, banking-session monitoring, clipboard manipulation, vishing overlays, and Remote Utilities deployment.

item.title: Phantom squatting: HalluSquatting / agentic botnet extension
item.description: Updated phantom-squatting guidance with Tel Aviv University / Technion / Intuit HalluSquatting research: predictable hallucinated repositories, skills, plugins, or other resources can be pre-registered by attackers and seeded with indirect prompt-injection content so coding agents with terminal or install privileges retrieve and execute attacker-supplied instructions. The page captures the reported Cursor, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot, Cline, Gemini CLI, and OpenClaw-family research demonstrations, plus defender controls for search-before-fetch grounding, approval gates, provenance checks, and clone/install telemetry.

item.title: UAT-7810 LONGLEASH ORB network expansion
item.description: Added Cisco Talos / The Hacker News coverage of China-nexus UAT-7810 expanding the LapDogs Operational Relay Box network with LONGLEASH, DOGLEASH, LEASHTEST, and JARLEASH tooling, including Ruckus and ASUS AiCloud router vulnerability pivots, MIPS embedded-device testing, relay/proxy behavior across HTTP, DNS, SOCKS, TCP, ICMP, and UDP, and defender guidance for exposed networking-device inventory, evidence preservation, and ORB relay hunts.

item.title: Linux GhostLock CVE-2026-43499 container escape
item.description: Added Nebula Security / The Hacker News coverage for GhostLock CVE-2026-43499, a Linux rtmutex / futex priority-inheritance stack use-after-free with public exploit code, reported 97% stable local-root exploitation, container-escape impact, Linux 2.6.39-era reachability, upstream Linux 7.1 fix context, and defender guidance for patch-and-reboot validation across container hosts, CI runners, shared Linux, and developer systems.

item.title: Agentic workflow trust-boundary failures: Rogue Agent Dialogflow runtime compromise
item.description: Updated agentic workflow trust-boundary guidance with Varonis Rogue Agent research: Dialogflow CX Playbook Code Blocks could overwrite files in a shared Google-managed Cloud Run runtime, causing other agents in the same GCP project to execute attacker logic, leak conversation data, bypass VPC Service Controls expectations through outbound egress, and expose IMDS tokens with limited logging visibility.

item.title: Vidar / XMRig Factory-v3 malvertising campaign
item.description: Added Unit 42 coverage of an April 2026 Vidar Stealer / XMRig malvertising campaign using cracked-software lures, password-protected .bin archives, Factory-v3 / UpdateFactory Go loaders, fake JustWatch and Bleacher Report Authenticode certificate branding, MpClient.dll sideloading, 491 MB null-byte file inflation, in-memory AmsiScanBuffer patching, Run-key / scheduled-task / Startup-folder persistence, and C2 / mining / credential-theft defender pivots.

item.title: RedWing mobile MaaS Android bank-fraud operation
item.description: Added Zimperium zLabs coverage of RedWing / Rokarolla, a Telegram-sold Android malware-as-a-service operation for mobile banking fraud. The pages capture fake app-store sideloading, APK builder and subscription model, Accessibility abuse, overlay credential theft, SMS / notification interception, VNC-style live control, camera / microphone and file access, silent *21* call forwarding, DDoS capability, and defender guidance for mobile fraud, MTD, and incident response.

item.title: RedWing
item.description: Added RedWing as an Android spyware / banking-trojan MaaS tool page, with Rokarolla and Oblivion lineage notes, Telegram builder model, fake app-store delivery, C2/admin-panel capabilities, overlay and Accessibility behavior, call-forwarding abuse, and mobile defender pivots.

item.title: DEBULL device-code phishing and GraphSpy post-exploitation
item.description: Added ZeroBEC coverage of DEBULL, a reusable Microsoft 365 device-code phishing tooling layer active in late June and early July 2026. The page captures collaboration-themed lures, a compromised Team_Meets first-stage website, DEBULL broker calls to generate and poll Microsoft Authentication Broker device codes, attacker-side sessions from 162.35.167[.]138 and 96.126.176[.]130, exposed DEBULL panel and PhaaS deployment artifacts, Turkish code-lineage markers, and the GraphSpy-Device post-authentication pivot for Microsoft Graph / Entra post-exploitation hunts.

item.title: GraphSpy
item.description: Added GraphSpy as a Microsoft Graph / Microsoft 365 post-exploitation tool pivot from ZeroBEC's DEBULL report. The page focuses defender hunts on GraphSpy-Device device-registration artifacts, Microsoft Authentication Broker / device-code sign-ins, OAuth token abuse, Microsoft Graph activity, mailbox / OneDrive / SharePoint / Teams access, and session revocation requirements after device-code phishing.

item.title: Kali365 device-code phishing expansion: ZeroBEC DEBULL / GraphSpy chain
item.description: Updated device-code phishing coverage with ZeroBEC's DEBULL / GraphSpy chain: legitimate Microsoft devicelogin flows, Microsoft Authentication Broker prompts, DEBULL broker endpoints, compromised collaboration-themed landing pages, GraphSpy-Device post-authentication artifacts, and defender pivots for Entra ID and Microsoft 365 incident response.

item.title: BeyondTrust RS / PRA CVE-2026-40138 / CVE-2026-40139 authentication bypass
item.description: Added coverage for BeyondTrust Remote Support and Privileged Remote Access BT26-03: CVE-2026-40138 and CVE-2026-40139 critical pre-authentication authentication-bypass flaws, plus CVE-2026-40140 denial-of-service and CVE-2026-40141 authenticated data-access risk. The page captures affected RS/PRA 25.3.2 and earlier versions, fixed 25.3.3 releases, configuration-dependent exposure, prior RS/PRA web-shell and backdoor exploitation context, and defender guidance for patching, exposure reduction, authentication-mode review, appliance-account audits, and compromise triage.

item.title: Cavern
item.description: Added Check Point Research coverage of Cavern, a modular .NET C2 and post-exploitation framework used by Iran-linked Cavern Manticore against Israeli government and IT-provider targets. The page captures RMM-driven WinDirStat DLL sideloading, uxtheme.dll agent behavior, n-HTCommp.dll HTTP/WebSocket transport, mixed .NET Framework / C++/CLI / NativeAOT anti-analysis architecture, AppDomain module isolation, DPAPI/SQL/LDAP/network/SMB/tunnel modules, C2 headers, and defender pivots for hospitalinstallation[.]com infrastructure and WinDirStat sideload artifacts.

item.title: Cavern Manticore
item.description: Added Check Point Research coverage of Cavern Manticore, an Iran/MOIS-linked cluster targeting Israeli government and IT-provider organizations with overlap to MuddyWater and Lyceum. The page captures RMM initial access, WinDirStat sideloading, Cavern framework deployment, PDB and infrastructure pivots, Cav3rn-to-Cavern lineage, and response guidance for preserving RMM, DLL, config, memory, and proxy telemetry.

item.title: Januscape KVM CVE-2026-53359 guest-to-host escape
item.description: Added coverage for Januscape CVE-2026-53359: a KVM/x86 shadow-MMU use-after-free disclosed by Hyunwoo Kim / V4bel after linux-distros embargo, used as a Google kvmCTF zero-day submission. The public PoC can panic x86 KVM hosts from a guest VM; the researcher says a full host-root escape exists but is withheld. The page captures nested-virtualization and multi-tenant-cloud risk, /dev/kvm LPE exposure, the June 2026 kernel fix commit, and defender guidance for patch validation, nested-virtualization restriction, host-panic triage, and co-resident guest secret scoping.

item.title: Gitea Docker CVE-2026-20896 probing
item.description: Added coverage for Gitea Docker CVE-2026-20896 active probing: official Docker images before and including 1.26.2 hard-coded REVERSE_PROXY_TRUSTED_PROXIES = *, so reverse-proxy authentication deployments with directly reachable container ports can accept attacker-supplied X-WEBAUTH-USER headers and impersonate known or guessable users. The page captures Sysdig's first observed probing 13 days after disclosure, ProtonVPN source IP 159.26.98[.]241, fixed version 1.26.3, and defender guidance for image upgrades, trusted-proxy allow-listing, direct-port exposure review, and source-control / CI credential rotation.

item.title: Kali365 device-code phishing expansion: Kaspersky legal-portal / Microsoft Identity Platform chain
item.description: Updated Kali365 / device-code phishing coverage with Kaspersky Securelist's July 6 report: law-firm email lures and password-protected PDFs routed victims through Microsoft redirector parameters, CAPTCHA-gated fake legal portals, clipboard-copied attacker user_code values, and Microsoft's legitimate device-login page. After the victim completed MFA, attackers obtained access, refresh, and ID tokens enabling mailbox read/send, OneDrive file exfiltration, and Teams conversation access.

item.title: QuimaRAT
item.description: Added LevelBlue SpiderLabs coverage of QuimaRAT, a commercialized Java RAT MaaS for Windows, Linux, and macOS. The page captures the builder/subscription model, Maven/JNA architecture, config.dat XOR key, 45.63.24[.]218:4447 C2, OS-specific persistence, Netty/WebSocket/Pastebin host-update behavior, plugin lifecycle, Windows fileless shellcode execution, protocol-only capability caveats, IOCs, and defender hunts for Java persistence plus plugin cache artifacts.

item.title: Agent skill marketplace poisoning: SkillCloak scanner evasion and SkillDetonate runtime auditing
item.description: Updated agent skill marketplace poisoning coverage with HKUST's SkillCloak / SkillDetonate paper. The page now captures measured bypass rates across eight scanners and 1,613 in-the-wild malicious skills, including structural obfuscation and self-extracting skill packing, plus defender guidance for sandbox detonation, synthetic secrets and canaries, information-flow telemetry, and treating static scanner verdicts as triage evidence rather than authorization.

item.title: ScreenConnect freeware / AsyncRAT SEO campaign
item.description: Added Kaspersky Securelist coverage of a large ScreenConnect-abuse campaign: spoofed freeware and game download sites appeared in search results, delivered ZIP archives with a renamed Microsoft-signed install.exe plus malicious install.res.1033.dll, silently installed ScreenConnect as Microsoft Update Service, and used PowerShell/VBScript staging, Defender exclusions, UAC prompt reduction, RegAsm process hollowing, and a two-minute MasterPackager.Updater scheduled task to deploy AsyncRAT. The page captures infrastructure clusters, selected IOCs, and defender hunts for RMM abuse.

item.title: FatFs CVE-2026-6682 to CVE-2026-6688 embedded-filesystem bug cluster
item.description: Added runZero Research coverage of seven FatFs vulnerabilities affecting embedded and firmware stacks: CVE-2026-6682 FAT32 mount integer overflow, CVE-2026-6687 exFAT label stack overflow, CVE-2026-6688 downstream long-file-name wrapper overflows, CVE-2026-6685 dirty-cache arithmetic wrap, CVE-2026-6683 exFAT sync/write divide-by-zero, CVE-2026-6686 stale-data exposure, and CVE-2026-6684 GPT scan denial of service. The page captures removable-media and OTA-update reachability, public PoC/harness availability, affected ecosystem examples, and defender inventory/firmware-update hardening guidance.

item.title: Kairos data-extortion government payment
item.description: Added Ransom-ISAC coverage of Kairos, a data-extortion actor that reportedly received a $1 million payment from a U.S. government body after claiming theft of more than 1.6 million files / 2 TB of data. The page captures the no-confirmed-encryptor caveat, $3 million initial demand, $100,000-to-$430,000 counteroffer path, roughly 9.44 BTC payment, Bybit / OKX / BELQI exchange-touchpoint leads, unverified brute-force access claim, non-verifiable proof-of-deletion warning, and public-sector defender guidance for evidence preservation, credential-root-cause analysis, and breach response.

item.title: @marketfront / @tqm-mfe dependency-confusion stealer
item.description: Added SafeDep coverage of the July 1, 2026 @marketfront / @tqm-mfe dependency-confusion stealer wave: 25 @marketfront packages at 7.0.0 plus @tqm-mfe/main at 5.4.7 and 5.5.0 reused the Internal package — Platform Engineering Team lure while evolving from broad environment collection into credential-file harvesting. The page captures package names, postinstall execution, RC4/XOR-hidden C2 configuration, gzip HTTPS POSTs to /api/v1/events with X-Secret, DNS resolver beaconing, private-registry fallback risk, and triage guidance for developer workstations and CI runners.

item.title: Linux Bad Epoll CVE-2026-46242 local privilege escalation
item.description: Added coverage for Bad Epoll CVE-2026-46242: a Linux kernel epoll/eventpoll race-condition use-after-free with public exploit material, kernelCTF exploitation context, Android-rooting relevance, Chrome renderer-sandbox chaining potential, and a Linux stable patch reference. The page captures defender guidance for kernel patch validation, reboot requirements, untrusted local-code exposure, CI/developer/container-host prioritization, and AI-era vulnerability-family closure caveats after Mythos found a sibling epoll race but missed Bad Epoll.

item.title: Citrix NetScaler CVE-2026-8451 memory overread
item.description: Added watchTowr Labs coverage of Citrix NetScaler CVE-2026-8451: a pre-authentication memory-overread issue in NetScaler ADC / Gateway SAML IdP configurations, patched June 30, 2026. The page captures affected branches, /saml/login and AuthnRequest parsing exposure, nsppe crash / denial-of-service risk, public validation-tooling urgency, and defender guidance for patching, SAML endpoint review, session invalidation, evidence preservation, and CitrixBleed-class runbooks.

item.title: Armored Likho BusySnake campaign
item.description: Added Kaspersky Securelist coverage of Armored Likho's active BusySnake Stealer campaign: spear-phishing archives against government and electric-power-sector targets in Russia, Kazakhstan, and Brazil; EXE and LNK first stages; AI-looking loader code; GitHub-hosted Python 3.12 / PyArmor payload staging; WindowsHelper scheduled-task persistence; browser credential and cookie theft; document, screenshot, clipboard, and key-string collection; and built-in reverse SSH tunneling.

item.title: NetNut / Popa residential proxy network disruption
item.description: Added Google Cloud / GTIG coverage of the NetNut / Popa residential proxy network disruption. The page captures Google's coordinated action with the FBI, Lumen, and partners; disabled Google-account C2 and Play Protect enforcement against NetNut SDK applications; GTIG estimates of at least 2 million devices; 316 distinct threat clusters observed using suspected NetNut exit nodes in one June 2026 week; Badbox 2.0 / Mirai-family context; reseller-capacity migration risk; and defender guidance for residential-proxy abuse, credential attacks, platform fraud controls, and consumer IoT exposure.

item.title: ToddyCat Umbrij Gmail OAuth operation
item.description: Added Kaspersky Securelist coverage of ToddyCat's Umbrij tool and Shadow Token via Remote Debug technique. The page captures Gmail access through Google API OAuth flows, headless Chrome/Edge launches against copied browser profiles, DevTools remote-debugging abuse, fake KasperskyEndpointSecurityEDRAvp scheduled-task masquerading, DLL sideloading through BDSubWiz.exe / VSTestVideoRecorder.exe / GoogleDesktop.exe, and defender pivots for endpoint plus Google Workspace OAuth telemetry.

item.title: JADEPUFFER Langflow agentic ransomware
item.description: Added Sysdig Threat Research Team coverage of JADEPUFFER, assessed as an end-to-end LLM-driven agentic ransomware operation. The page captures Langflow CVE-2025-3248 initial access, adaptive/self-narrating payloads, cloud and container reconnaissance, cron beaconing to 45.131.66[.]106:4444, pivoting to exposed MySQL and Alibaba Nacos, CVE-2021-29441/default-JWT-key context, encryption of 1,342 Nacos configuration items, and defender guidance for AI workflow exposure, credential scoping, and database-recovery planning. FortiBleed coverage was also updated with SOCRadar's INC/Lynx ransomware-link follow-up.

item.title: Adobe ColdFusion APSB26-68 CVE bonanza
item.description: Added watchTowr Labs coverage of Adobe ColdFusion APSB26-68: ColdFusion 2025 Update 9 and earlier and ColdFusion 2023 Update 20 and earlier received fixes for a large vulnerability cluster including arbitrary file read/write, file upload path traversal, CKEditor file-manager directory listing, and additional XSLT SSRF / XXE / file-write classes. The page captures CVE pivots, CFIDE / FILEIO hunt paths, exposure-reduction guidance, and post-exploitation review steps for ColdFusion estates.

item.title: Argo CD repo-server unauthenticated RCE
item.description: Added Synacktiv coverage of an unpatched, no-CVE unauthenticated code-execution path in Argo CD repo-server. The page captures the internal gRPC plus Redis reachability prerequisite, arbitrary manifest deployment / cluster-compromise impact, Helm NetworkPolicy default-risk caveat, and defender guidance for Argo CD network segmentation, Kubernetes audit review, and credential rotation.

item.title: Progress Kemp LoadMaster CVE-2026-8037 active exploitation attempts
item.description: Updated Progress Kemp LoadMaster CVE-2026-8037 coverage with eSentire TRU / The Hacker News reporting that exploitation attempts began June 29, 2026. eSentire said the observed attempts failed with no post-compromise activity, but reported attacker IPs 192.42.116[.]58, 192.42.116[.]105, and 146.70.139[.]154; the page now treats exposed /accessv2 API surfaces as actively probed and adds retrospective hunt guidance.

item.title: ClickFix CPaaS API-driven payload delivery
item.description: Added Bert-Jan Pals / The Hacker News coverage of API-driven ClickFix payload delivery: roughly 3,000 live payloads and multiple platforms showed ClickFix operators using payload-as-a-service backends, localized fake-CAPTCHA flows, Windows Terminal execution paths, unique dynamic PowerShell obfuscation, and a Downloads-folder archive/script method that reduces directly malicious clipboard text. The page captures CPaaS API behavior, LOLBin pivots, domains, and defender hunts for browser-to-clipboard-to-Terminal execution chains.

item.title: Azure CLI LSHIY password-spray campaign
item.description: Added Huntress / The Hacker News coverage of an ongoing Azure CLI password-spray campaign: activity from LSHIY LLC / AS32167 IPv6 space produced more than 81 million login attempts from June 12-26, 2026 and compromised at least 78 Microsoft accounts across 64 organizations. The page captures ROPC token-grant abuse, Conditional Access and MFA scoping gaps, 2a0a:d683::/32 infrastructure, and defender pivots for Entra ID sign-in telemetry, Azure CLI restrictions, ROPC blocking, policy-audit coverage, session revocation, and credential rotation.

item.title: Lazarus-linked Rollup polyfill npm malware
item.description: Added JFrog Security Research coverage of a Lazarus-linked npm cluster masquerading as Rollup polyfill tooling. The page captures six affected package names, import-time second-stage installation through swift-parse-stream / quirky-token, JSONKeeper model-field evaluation, 216.126.236.244 remote-access and upload endpoints, browser and cryptocurrency-wallet theft, node-pty / Socket.IO operator access, and defender pivots for package masquerading, CommonJS-vs-ESM review, silent npm installs, and developer-workstation credential rotation.

item.title: Phantom squatting AI-hallucinated domains
item.description: Added Unit 42 coverage for phantom squatting: adversaries can register domains that LLMs hallucinate as plausible official portals, APIs, documentation hosts, or service endpoints, then receive traffic from AI assistants or autonomous agents that treat generated URLs as authoritative. The page captures Unit 42's 913-brand / 2.1-million-URL measurement, 13,229 confirmed malicious URLs, roughly 250,000 unregistered phantom domains, reported 18-51 day registration-prediction windows, Montana Empire phishing-kit case, and defender pivots for AI-generated URL allowlisting, registration monitoring, and developer/agent workflow controls.

item.title: Silent Swap Google Notes crypto clipper
item.description: Added McAfee Labs / The Hacker News coverage for Silent Swap, a cryptocurrency-clipper campaign that uses unsigned .NET and Golang installers to force-load a malicious Chromium extension masquerading as Google Notes. The page captures BaseZipInstaller behavior, browser profile Secure Preferences / Preferences tampering, integrity-value recalculation to bypass normal extension installation, EtherHiding blockchain C2/dead-drop resolution, dynamic wallet-address substitution with hardcoded fallback, and defender pivots for browser-extension inventory, profile-file monitoring, clipboard risk, and cryptocurrency transaction verification.

item.title: RustDuck
item.description: Added QiAnXin XLab coverage for RustDuck, a two-stage DDoS botnet family active since February 2026 that is evolving from C toward Rust. The page captures weak Telnet/SSH password plus IoT, Android ADB, Jenkins, YARN, ThinkPHP, and historical-CVE propagation; Loader + Core variant markers; SSL-looking AES-GCM C2; dynamic C2 update and hot-update commands; and defender pivots for edge/IoT fleets, overlay-config extraction, dynamic-DNS C2, and flood-traffic detection.

item.title: MCP tool-description poisoning
item.description: Added Microsoft / The Hacker News coverage of MCP tool-description poisoning: an already-approved third-party tool can hide instructions in mutable description metadata that an acting AI agent treats as trusted planning context, causing legitimate-looking data pulls and external tool calls such as exfiltrating the last 30 unpaid invoices. The page captures the tool-metadata supply-chain boundary, related tool-poisoning research, and defender guidance for metadata re-approval, least agency, per-agent identities, DLP, and tool-call logging.

item.title: BioShocking AI-browser context manipulation
item.description: Updated AI-augmented adversary operations with LayerX BioShocking research: a malicious page can frame an agentic browser task as a game, manipulate the agent's operating context, and cause it to copy credentials or other data from authenticated sites such as GitHub without treating the action as a real-world safety violation. Added affected-product context for ChatGPT Atlas, Perplexity Comet, Fellou, Genspark Browser, Sigma Browser, and the Claude Chrome plugin plus defender guidance for step-up confirmation, scoped browser profiles, and agent navigation monitoring.

item.title: SimpleHelp CVE-2026-48558 TaskWeaver / Djinn Stealer chain
item.description: Updated SimpleHelp CVE-2026-48558 coverage with Blackpoint Cyber / The Hacker News intrusion details: an unknown actor used a forged SimpleHelp technician session to deploy TaskWeaver, a heavily obfuscated Node.js loader delivered as jquery.js and executed through node.exe, then delivered Djinn Stealer to harvest cross-platform browser, cloud, source-control, package-registry, infrastructure-tooling, AI-assistant, SSH, and cryptocurrency secrets. Added dedicated TaskWeaver and Djinn Stealer tool pages plus defender pivots for SimpleHelp session correlation, Node.js execution from RMM tooling, a.dev-tunnels[.]com, and 96.126.130[.]126:58942.

item.title: Oracle E-Business Suite CVE-2026-46817 exploitation
item.description: Added Oracle E-Business Suite CVE-2026-46817 exploitation coverage: a critical unauthenticated HTTP issue in Oracle Payments / File Transmission affecting EBS 12.2.3 through 12.2.15. The page captures Oracle/NVD CVSS 9.8 details, Defused Cyber honeypot exploitation telemetry reported by The Hacker News, no-known-public-PoC caveat, and defender triage for Oracle Payments exposure, EBS logs, application accounts, payment workflow changes, and adjacent Oracle-app exploitation risk.

item.title: Progress Kemp LoadMaster CVE-2026-8037 pre-auth RCE
item.description: Added watchTowr Labs coverage for Progress Kemp LoadMaster CVE-2026-8037: a pre-authentication RCE path reachable when the LoadMaster API is enabled. The page captures affected GA v7.2.63.1-and-older and LTSF v7.2.54.17-and-older versions named by watchTowr, the /accessv2 apiuser uninitialized-heap-to-command-injection mechanics, companion Progress bulletin reference to CVE-2026-33691, and defender triage for API exposure, /accessv2 requests, appliance configuration review, and credential/certificate rotation.

item.title: Mustang Panda ZOHOMURK / MINIRECON India campaigns
item.description: Added Acronis Threat Research Unit coverage of two Mustang Panda espionage campaigns against Indian government and hydropower-sector targets: hydropower and India-Taiwan cooperation lures, Solid PDF Creator DLL sideloading through hidden SolidPDFCreator.dll, SHARDLOADER, MINIRECON with TONESHELL overlap, ZOHOMURK Zoho WorkDrive C2/tasking/exfiltration, SolidPDFPcl2Bmp scheduled-task persistence, couldinstallup[.]com WebSocket C2, and defender pivots for endpoint plus SaaS/OAuth telemetry.

item.title: SimpleHelp CVE-2026-48558 authentication-bypass exploitation
item.description: Added CISA KEV coverage for SimpleHelp CVE-2026-48558: an OIDC authentication-bypass vulnerability where vulnerable deployments accept login identity tokens without verifying cryptographic signatures, allowing a remote unauthenticated attacker to forge identity claims and obtain a fully authenticated technician session; in some configurations, MFA may also be bypassed. The page captures SimpleHelp 5.5.15-and-earlier / 6.0 prerelease update guidance, SimpleHelp 5.5.16 and 6.0 RC2 fixes, CISA's July 2 remediation due date, and defender triage for technician sessions, OIDC/IdP telemetry, remote-support activity, and credential rotation.

item.title: Perplexity AI-spoofing Chromium extension search hijacker
item.description: Added Microsoft Defender Security Research coverage of a malicious Chromium extension, Search for perplexity ai, that spoofed Perplexity AI branding, forced itself as the default search provider through chrome_settings_overrides, used Manifest V3 declarativeNetRequest permissions, and routed full Omnibox searches plus real-time suggestions through perplexity-ai[.]online before redirecting users to expected search providers. The page captures extension ID flkebkiofojicogddingbdmcmkpbplcd, the removed Chrome Web Store exposure, installation URL extension.tilda[.]ws/perplexityai, and defender pivots for browser-extension inventory, proxy/DNS hunts, and extension-policy review.

item.title: DCloud Uni-App scam infrastructure ecosystem
item.description: Added Infoblox Threat Intel coverage of the DCloud Uni-App scam infrastructure ecosystem: 236,493 DCloud-built investment-scam second-level domains observed since mid-2022, post-RainbowEx growth to roughly 15,000 newly observed sites per month at peak, fake crypto exchanges, wallet drainers, WhatsApp phishing, scambling/fake gambling, brand impersonation, bulletproof-hosted evasive variants, and offline fraud crossover through RainbowEx, Lightning Shared Scooter Co., and Yuechi Shared Technology.

item.title: StegoAd Edge extension steganography campaign
item.description: Added Microsoft Edge Extensions Security Team coverage for StegoAd: 119 malicious Edge Add-ons extensions across 90+ disposable developer accounts with up to 2.6 million installs, delayed and probabilistic execution, DevTools-aware evasion, server-side request validation, JavaScript hidden in PNG / WebP / WOFF2 image and font assets, ad injection, affiliate hijacking, Google credential and second-factor interception, WordPress administrator credential harvesting, bulk cookie exfiltration, and a browser-session remote-code-execution backdoor.

item.title: Operation DragonReturn India tax-season DcRAT campaign
item.description: Added Seqrite coverage for Operation DragonReturn: an active China-nexus espionage campaign impersonating India's Income Tax Department / Ministry of Finance during AY2026-27 filing season. The page captures the govtop.one lure, fake Common_Offline_Utility_ITR-1_to_4_AY2026-27.zip download, MixedSvc / Windows Mixed Reality Service persistence, background.jpg payload-container staging, svchost.exe process injection, AMSI patching, in-memory .NET loading, TLS-encrypted MessagePack C2, desktop capture capability, and defender hunts for taxpayer, tax-professional, and corporate-finance endpoints.

item.title: Banana RAT / SHADOW-WATER-063 Brazilian banking fraud
item.description: Added Trend Micro coverage for Banana RAT / SHADOW-WATER-063: a Brazilian Portuguese, financially motivated banking-fraud operation using WhatsApp or phishing lures, PowerShell fileless execution, a FastAPI polymorphic payload-generation pool, hidden scheduled-task persistence, custom TCP/443 AES-encrypted C2, screen streaming, operator-driven input control, fake banking/security overlays, and Pix QR-code interception against Brazilian financial institutions and localized cryptocurrency exchanges.

item.title: Russian intelligence Signal backup-key phishing
item.description: Updated Russian Intelligence Services commercial-messaging phishing coverage with SBU's June 27 notice: Russian services are systematically targeting messenger accounts used by Ukrainian, European, and U.S. officials, military personnel, politicians, activists, and personal Ukrainian accounts through fake support-team texts, verification-code/PIN/password theft, QR-code account-linking lures, and recovery-key requests. The page retains FBI/CISA's Signal Backup Recovery Key guidance for UNC5792 and UNC4221 and adds SBU-derived active-session and QR-code defensive pivots.

item.title: Immobiliare Labs Backstage plugins npm compromise
item.description: Added StepSecurity coverage for the June 26 Immobiliare Labs Backstage plugin compromise: four npm packages across GitLab and LDAP Backstage integrations received malicious patch releases with Miasma-style Phantom Gyp execution through binding.gyp, a 5 MB index.js payload, Bun v1.3.13 staging, Runner.Worker memory scraping, cloud / package-registry / password-manager credential theft, AI-assistant persistence, and apparent npm / PyPI worming functions. The page captures affected package versions, hunt pivots, and containment guidance for platform-engineering CI and developer endpoints.

item.title: Linux DirtyClone CVE-2026-43503 local privilege escalation
item.description: Added JFrog Security Research coverage for DirtyClone / CVE-2026-43503: a DirtyFrag-family Linux kernel local privilege-escalation flaw where local users who can acquire CAP_NET_ADMIN, often through unprivileged user namespaces, can manipulate shared page-cache memory through socket-buffer processing paths to gain root. The page captures the incomplete DirtyFrag patch-chain risk, XFRM/IPsec and skb Copy-on-Write context, Debian / Ubuntu / Fedora exposure notes, mitigation options such as kernel updates, user-namespace restrictions, and esp4 / esp6 / rxrpc module review, plus hunt guidance for shared CI, Kubernetes, container-host, and multi-user Linux fleets.

item.title: Turla STOCKSTAY backdoor operations
item.description: Added Google Threat Intelligence Group coverage for Turla's STOCKSTAY backdoor: a multi-component .NET Windows implant developed since at least December 2022 and used against Ukrainian government / military organizations and Italian foreign-policy-adjacent targets. The update adds Turla actor, STOCKSTAY tool, and operations pages covering WebSocket C2, WM_COPYDATA IPC, STOCKBROKER / STOCKMARKET / STOCKTRADER / MARKETMAKER components, KAZUAR / K1MORPHER overlap, malicious GPO deployment, Italy-themed MSI lure, Ukrainian RDP phishing, compromised drs.gov.ua staging, and defender hunts for encrypted stock-market-themed configs, run keys, and business-hours C2.

item.title: CL-STA-1062 Southeast Asia government and energy intrusions
item.description: Added Unit 42 coverage for CL-STA-1062: a Chinese-speaking espionage cluster, assessed with high confidence as overlapping Cisco Talos UAT-7237, targeting Southeast Asian government and state-owned critical energy entities. The update adds a CL-STA-1062 actor page, TinyRCT tool page, and campaign page covering ASPX web shells, SoftEther VPN / VNT / yuze tunneling, RAR staging, AppDomainManager injection through chrome_setup.zip, PerfWatson2.exe, AES-128-CBC HTTP C2, GoogleUpdaterTaskSystem scheduled-task persistence, and defender hunts for web-shell-led staging and renamed tunnel tooling.

item.title: Leo Platform npm Miasma-style compromise: Sonatype affected-package clarification
item.description: Updated Leo Platform / Miasma coverage with Sonatype's June 25 clarification: Sonatype aligned the llxlr-published hexo-deployer-wrangler, hexo-shoka-swiper, and prism-silq packages with the same payload-bearing campaign, assigned advisory pivot Sonatype-2026-004261, and cautioned that leo-connector-common@4.0.11-rc, leo-connector-postgres@4.0.19-beta, and leo-connector-entity-table@3.0.22-rc appeared in some early lists but did not appear to carry the confirmed Miasma payload in Sonatype's current analysis.

item.title: PTC Windchill / FlexPLM CVE-2026-12569 exploitation
item.description: Added CISA KEV coverage for PTC Windchill PDMLink and PTC FlexPLM CVE-2026-12569: a critical unauthenticated remote-code-execution vulnerability described as untrusted-data deserialization / improper input validation, added to KEV on June 25, 2026 with a June 28 remediation due date. The page captures affected-version context from NVD, PTC CVSS 4.0 9.3 severity, active-exploitation implications, and defender guidance for urgent exposure review, patching, log preservation, application-server triage, and credential rotation.

item.title: Leo Platform npm Miasma-style compromise: Socket Go/source-repository expansion
item.description: Updated Leo Platform / Miasma coverage with Socket's June 25 follow-up: the wave expanded from 20 StepSecurity-listed Leo/RStreams npm packages to 23 npm packages with llxlr-published hexo-deployer-wrangler, hexo-shoka-swiper, and prism-silq, plus a related Verana Blockchain Go source-archive poisoning case. The update adds RevokeAndItGoesKaboom / Alright Lets See If This Works campaign markers, Verana .claude and .vscode hook pivots, Bun-staged source-repository execution risk, and repository-cleanup guidance beyond npm package removal.

item.title: Adblock for YouTube BadBlocker remote-script injection risk
item.description: Added Island Security Research coverage for Adblock for YouTube / BadBlocker: a Chrome Web Store extension with more than 11 million installs, broad <all_urls> permissions, weak youtube.com substring gating, 24-hour remote rule fetches from api.adblock-for-youtube.com, and server-selected scripletsRules that can drive chrome.scripting.executeScript in the page MAIN world. Island did not observe active malicious payload delivery; the page frames this as a latent high-blast-radius browser-session execution risk with defender pivots for extension inventory, managed-browser policy, and endpoint/proxy telemetry.

item.title: Backdoor.Mistic / KongTuke ModeloRAT activity
item.description: Added coverage for Broadcom / Symantec Threat Hunter Team's Backdoor.Mistic report: a stealthy Windows backdoor used since April 2026 and possibly linked to Woodgnat / KongTuke access-broker activity. The page captures Mistic / MLTBackdoor execution through MpExtMs.exe DLL sideloading, version.dll hooks, EndpointDlp.dll in-memory loading, fake-login credential theft, ModeloRAT / WinPython / RC4 C2 tradecraft, ClickFix and compromised-WordPress TDS context, Qilin ransomware access-broker risk, and defender hunts for sideloaded Microsoft-looking components and portable Python persistence.

item.title: macOS.Gaslight Rust backdoor
item.description: Added SentinelOne macOS.Gaslight coverage: a DPRK-aligned Rust macOS implant with Telegram Bot API polling C2, AES-GCM over certificate-pinned TLS, bot-token self-redaction, interactive shell commands, LaunchAgent persistence under com.apple.system.services.activity, sleep-prevention behavior, browser and login.keychain-db collection, and a staged Python stealer runtime. The page also captures Gaslight's 3.5 KB analyst-targeting prompt-injection block with 38 fabricated system messages aimed at disrupting LLM-assisted malware triage.

item.title: Leo Platform npm Miasma-style compromise
item.description: Added coverage for StepSecurity's June 25, 2026 Leo Platform npm compromise: 20 packages were maliciously published in a three-second burst on June 24 with the same Miasma-style Phantom Gyp binding.gyp install hook, ROT-N / AES-128-GCM / obfuscator.io layering, Bun v1.3.13 runtime download, GitHub Actions Runner.Worker memory scraping, GitHub dead-drop exfiltration, npm bypass_2fa worming, workflow injection, and runner sudoers modification. The page captures affected package/version pairs, hunt pivots, response steps, and an attribution caveat for likely same payload factory versus copycat reuse.

item.title: StrikeShark SharkLoader / Cobalt Strike campaign
item.description: Added coverage for Kaspersky's June 2026 StrikeShark report: a SharkLoader campaign delivering Cobalt Strike Beacon after internet-facing application exploitation or custom droppers disguised as Cisco AnyConnect, Google Update, or decoy PDFs. The page captures old edge-vulnerability exposure, web-shell post-exploitation, copied SystemSettings.exe DLL sideloading, DscCoreR.mui and SyncRes.dat reflective loading, API-hooked in-memory Beacon execution, registry Run keys, scheduled-task persistence, victimology, and Kaspersky's no-attribution caveat.

item.title: GitHub Actions deployment poisoning: Cordyceps CI/CD composition flaws
item.description: Updated the GitHub Actions deployment poisoning pattern with Novee Security's Cordyceps CI/CD workflow-composition research: The Hacker News reported Novee's scan of roughly 30,000 high-impact repositories found more than 300 fully exploitable cases where untrusted pull-request comments, branch names, artifacts, or metadata could cross into privileged automation. The page adds reported examples involving Microsoft Azure Sentinel, Google adk-samples, Apache Doris, Cloudflare Workers SDK, and Python Black, and focuses defender review on trust-boundary validation before secret-bearing or write-token workflow steps.

item.title: codfish semantic-release-action tag compromise
item.description: Added coverage for StepSecurity's June 24, 2026 codfish/semantic-release-action GitHub Actions compromise: seven version tags were reportedly force-retargeted to malicious commit 6b9501e, converting the action from Docker to composite, installing Bun with oven-sh/setup-bun@v2, running an if: always() obfuscated JavaScript payload, stealing GitHub OIDC tokens and PATs, encrypting collected material with AES-128-GCM, and attempting repository backdoor propagation. The page focuses on malicious-window workflow-run triage, Bun/action-path hunt pivots, tag-retargeting controls, and credential rotation for release runners.

item.title: html-to-gutenberg / fetch-page-assets VS Code blockchain stealer
item.description: Added coverage for JFrog Security Research's June 24, 2026 hijacked npm package report: html-to-gutenberg@4.2.11 and fetch-page-assets@1.2.9 avoided npm lifecycle hooks by hiding a VS Code runOn folderOpen task that launched JavaScript disguised as public/fonts/fa-solid-400.woff2. The page captures Tron/Aptos/BSC blockchain dead-drop staging, Sec-V-based C2 selection, socket.io backdoor control, Python credential and wallet theft, runtime artifacts, and defender guidance for treating trusted-workspace editor tasks as package execution surfaces.

item.title: StealC / Amadey infrastructure disruption
item.description: Added coverage for Microsoft's June 24, 2026 StealC and Amadey disruption: Microsoft Digital Crimes Unit, Europol, and industry partners acted against more than 200 malicious C2 domains and IPs. The page captures StealC browser, wallet, cookie, Outlook, WinSCP, screenshot, file-grab, App-Bound Encryption bypass, and loader behavior; Amadey scheduled-task persistence, plugin, SOCKS, RDP, hidden-admin, VNC, and follow-on malware capabilities; and defender guidance to treat infections as identity and credential incidents rather than endpoint-only malware cleanup.

item.title: Cisco Unified CM CVE-2026-20230 file-write exploitation
item.description: Added coverage for Cisco Unified CM / Unified CM SME CVE-2026-20230: a WebDialer-gated unauthenticated SSRF flaw that Cisco says can write files to the underlying operating system and later support root escalation. The page captures Cisco's no-workaround advisory, WebDialer disablement mitigation, fixed release 14SU6 and release-15 COP / 15SU5 guidance, SSD Secure Disclosure technical publication context, and The Hacker News / Defused Cyber telemetry of PoC-derived file-write exploitation against decoys.

item.title: Thailand healthcare RAR / Python stealer campaign
item.description: Added coverage for Seqrite's June 2026 Thailand healthcare campaign: Ministry of Health and medical-workflow lures delivered malicious RAR archives, Rouki-obfuscated batch loaders, GitHub-hosted payloads, Startup-folder persistence through WindowSecuryt.bat, a bundled Python runtime under C:\Users\Public\Desktops, sim.py information stealing, browser-data collection, and Telegram Bot API exfiltration attempts. The page keeps Seqrite's no-attribution caveat and defender hunts for GitHub script staging, Startup-folder batch files, C:\Users\Public\Desktops.zip, and unexpected Python execution on healthcare endpoints.

item.title: xlabs_v1 DDoS-for-hire IoT botnet
item.description: Added Hunt.io coverage for xlabs_v1, a Mirai-derived DDoS-for-hire IoT botnet exposed through an unauthenticated debug-build staging directory. The page captures ADB-on-TCP/5555 infection, 21 game-server-focused flood variants including RakNet and OpenVPN-shaped UDP, Speedtest-based bandwidth tiering through 8,192 parallel sockets, /bin/bash process masquerading, TCP/26721 fallback re-entry, and defender guidance for IoT / Android-derived device triage.

item.title: WhatsApp VBScript ManageEngine RMM campaign
item.description: Added coverage for Kaspersky's June 2026 WhatsApp VBScript campaign: compromised WhatsApp accounts send finance-themed .vbs / .vbe attachments that execute through Windows Script Host, stage hidden directories under C:\Users\Public\Documents, download secondary scripts, attempt UAC prompt reduction, and silently install a preconfigured ManageEngine Endpoint Central agent for attacker remote access. The page keeps Kaspersky's low-confidence Chinese-speaking-operator caveat, ValleyRAT / Gh0st RAT infrastructure-overlap caveat, and defender hunts for WhatsApp-spawned WScript, suspicious Endpoint Central enrollment, and script-driven ZIP / msiexec activity.

item.title: Agent skill marketplace poisoning: Unit 42 OpenClaw marketplace follow-up
item.description: Updated the agent skill marketplace poisoning pattern with Unit 42's June 23, 2026 OpenClaw / ClawHub follow-up: five reportedly unblocked skills spanning ClawHavoc-style macOS infostealer delivery, 22 MB README padding to evade scanner thresholds, runtime affiliate-link injection through remote JSON, and agentic Solana token front-running. The page adds defender guidance for inspecting oversized files, prerequisite paste-site commands, mutable remote JSON / documentation dependencies, and outbound domains that do not match the skill's declared purpose.

item.title: Ubiquiti UniFi OS and Lantronix EDS5000 KEV exploitation
item.description: Added concise CISA KEV coverage for June 23, 2026 edge and ICS management-plane exploitation: Ubiquiti UniFi OS CVE-2026-34908 / CVE-2026-34909 / CVE-2026-34910 and Lantronix EDS5000 CVE-2025-67038. The pages focus on UniFi OS traversal / command-injection risk with PwnDefend-reported Mirai-style honeypot exploitation, Lantronix failed-auth username command injection with root privileges, fixed-version guidance, exposure control, failed-auth/traversal log review, and root-command-execution triage.

item.title: Agent skill marketplace poisoning: AIR external-document skill swap
item.description: Updated the agent skill marketplace poisoning pattern with AIR Security's June 2026 public experiment: a plausible AI-agent skill passed static scanner and reputation checks by keeping the submitted package clean while outsourcing setup instructions to mutable external documentation. AIR reported roughly 26,000 affected agents and changed the linked content after distribution so the agent would download and run a demonstration script that sent only an email address. The page caveats AIR's vendor-reported scale claims and adds defender guidance for treating external docs, setup guides, and product-adjacent domains as part of the reviewed skill artifact.

item.title: wshu.net npm credential-stealer campaign
item.description: Added coverage for SafeDep's June 23, 2026 wshu.net npm campaign: 15 plausible utility packages across 13 throwaway scopes and 64 versions delivered obfuscated postinstall JavaScript loaders and a cross-platform Rust infostealer. The page captures scrubbed latest tags, runtime execution in @petitcode/eb-retry and @briskforge/envcheck, GitHub Releases second-stage delivery, wallet / browser / cloud / SSH / developer-token theft, user-level systemd persistence, Telegram C2, and defender guidance for historical-version review, endpoint triage, and credential rotation.

item.title: Agent skill marketplace poisoning: developer-environment update
item.description: Updated the agent skill marketplace poisoning pattern with Snyk's June 23, 2026 developer-environment findings and JFrog's agent-plugin repository guidance. The page now treats MCP servers, skills, hooks, slash commands, subagents, and plugin manifests as executable supply-chain inputs on developer endpoints, captures Snyk's observed MCP / skill / prompt-injection risk metrics, and adds governance guidance for immutable reviewed plugin artifacts, endpoint inventory, and telemetry before code reaches CI.

item.title: Langflow CVE-2026-33017 cryptominer SSH worm
item.description: Added coverage for Trend Micro's June 23, 2026 Langflow CVE-2026-33017 cryptominer campaign: exposed unauthenticated Langflow endpoints run a Python os.system curl-to-shell payload, stage isp.sh and lambsys, deploy a customized XMRig miner, evict rival miners, add cron and init_rmount watchdog persistence, and attempt SSH lateral movement through keys, known_hosts, and agent sockets. The page treats compromise as an AI-infrastructure and SSH-key scoping incident, not just host-level mining noise.

item.title: Fake-reputation crypto clipboard hijacker
item.description: Added coverage for Check Point Research's June 17, 2026 fake-reputation clipboard-hijacker campaign: a Rust Windows and macOS cryptocurrency clipper distributed through a phishing hub, GitHub and SourceForge projects, AI-narrated YouTube videos, crypto forums, news-site promotion, and manipulated-looking VirusTotal sentiment. The page captures fake social-proof mechanics, Windows and macOS persistence, wallet-address replacement, and defender guidance for treating stars, downloads, comments, and safe votes as weak signals without provenance and behavioral validation.

item.title: Cloud bucket namespace hijacking
item.description: Added a reusable cloud-storage pattern from Unit 42's June 22, 2026 global namespace bucket-hijacking research: deleted and recreated object-storage destinations can redirect continuing data streams from Cloud Logging, Pub/Sub, Storage Transfer Service, S3 replication, Amazon Data Firehose, and Azure Monitor diagnostics. The page captures the no-known-in-the-wild caveat, cross-cloud mechanics, storage-delete least privilege, data perimeter controls, deletion alerts, and destination-owner verification.

item.title: AI-agent memory poisoning
item.description: Added a reusable defender pattern from Microsoft's June 22, 2026 AI memory guidance: persistent agent memory turns one-shot prompt-injection risk into delayed, stateful influence over later tool calls. The page captures memory poisoning, delayed tool execution, provenance requirements, write-time and retrieval-time risk checks, memory audit logging, Defender / Sentinel MemoryUpdated telemetry, and incident-response guidance for preserving and removing poisoned memory.

item.title: Storm-2603 parallel SharePoint ransomware intrusion
item.description: Added coverage for Microsoft Incident Response's June 22, 2026 Cyberattack Series No. 9: a ransomware investigation where Storm-2603 SharePoint-focused activity overlapped with a second unnamed actor in the same environment. The page captures SharePoint vulnerability targeting and local-file-inclusion probing, Velociraptor SYSTEM execution, Cloudflare Tunnel, Zoho Assist, VS Code Remote SSH, rogue administrator creation, NSecKrnl.sys BYOVD defense evasion, DLL sideloading, NTDS.dit archive theft, and incident-response guidance for splitting parallel activity streams before attribution.

item.title: postcss-minify-selector-parser npm RAT
item.description: Added coverage for JFrog Security Research's June 22, 2026 PostCSS-themed npm package cluster: postcss-minify-selector-parser, postcss-minify-selector, and aes-decode-runner-pro. The page captures import-time JavaScript execution through index.js and src/config/defaults.js, an AES-decoded PowerShell downloader, nvidiadriver[.]net Windows bundle staging, a bundled Python 3.10 / Nuitka RAT, Chrome credential theft, HKCU Run persistence, and concrete Windows developer-endpoint hunting pivots.

item.title: FFmpeg PixelSmash CVE-2026-8461 media-file RCE
item.description: Added coverage for JFrog Security Research's PixelSmash disclosure: CVE-2026-8461, a heap out-of-bounds write in FFmpeg's MagicYUV decoder that can be triggered by crafted AVI, MKV, or MOV media processed by desktop players, thumbnailers, media servers, preview providers, cloud transcoders, and bundled FFmpeg dependencies. The page captures Jellyfin and Nextcloud exploitation examples, the ASLR-disabled RCE caveat, MagicYUV decoder checks, FFmpeg 8.1.2 / rebuild mitigation guidance, and triage for automatic media-processing workflows.

item.title: AryStinger legacy-router recon proxy network
item.description: Added coverage for QiAnXin XLab's AryStinger report: a legacy-router and NAS bot family that compromises RTL819X-era Linksys and D-Link routers via CVE-2013-3307 / CVE-2016-5681 and QNAP Malware Remover via CVE-2025-11837 to build reconnaissance, tunneling, and proxy infrastructure. The page captures the 4,300+ RTL819X-router measurement, D-Link DIR-850L concentration, Protobuf plus XOR C2, syswapd0 artifacts, Dropbear / gs-netcat persistence, and defender pivots for retiring unsupported edge devices and hunting ajb8 / dataexplore infrastructure.

item.title: MYRA RAT
item.description: Added coverage for SafeDep's June 21, 2026 MYRA / apintergrationpost report: a public npm package that installs a Linux RAT with root-required lifecycle scripts, native LD_PRELOAD and memfd components, cron and profile.d persistence, systemd-userdbd masquerading, HMAC-authenticated TCP C2, and live screen-streaming support. The page includes npm registry version context through 4.1.0 and concrete Linux hunt pivots for files, processes, cron, loader paths, apt logs, and network indicators.

item.title: Oracle PeopleSoft CVE-2026-35273: PSIGW / PSEMHUB chain analysis
item.description: Updated PeopleSoft CVE-2026-35273 coverage with Trend Micro's PSIGW / PSEMHUB technical chain: unauthenticated Integration Gateway SSRF to localhost PSEMHUB, validateClient bypass, envmetadata staging, Java XMLDecoder deserialization on web-tier restart, in-JVM execution without child-process or beacon telemetry, and new hunt pivots for IBRequest loopback URLs, XML writes, restart correlation, JSP web shells, and outbound SMB coercion.

item.title: UNC6508
item.description: Added GTIG's UNC6508 reporting: a high-confidence PRC-nexus espionage cluster targeting North American academic, medical, military, and health-policy organizations through REDCap compromise, INFINITERED credential harvesting / backdoor persistence, and mail content-compliance rule abuse for silent BCC exfiltration. The page captures REDCap legacy-version risk, INFINITERED host artifacts, administrator credential replay, OBF network use, and SaaS mail-control-plane hunting guidance.

item.title: SprySOCKS Windows backdoor variants
item.description: Added ESET's June 2026 FishMonger / SprySOCKS research: two Windows variants, WIN_DRV and WIN_PLUS, tied to government-sector activity in Honduras, Taiwan, Thailand, and Pakistan. The new tool and actor pages capture kernel-driver stealth, TCP traffic diversion to hidden listeners, Fonts-directory encrypted containers, transient fsdiskbit.sys / msidiskserver driver loading, C2 protocol support, and caveated UEFI bootkit telemetry.

channel.title: threat.wiki
channel.description: Threat intelligence notes, group profiles, named-person records, and defensive guidance.

item.title: FortiBleed Fortinet credential exposure: Arctic Wolf impact-count update
item.description: Updated FortiBleed coverage with Arctic Wolf's June 17, 2026 bulletin, which summarized SOCRadar and Kevin Beaumont / Hudson Rock reporting on more than 30,791 confirmed working Fortinet credentials, an estimated 75,000 affected devices across 194 countries, and the need to force administrator-password rotation so upgraded FortiOS deployments do not retain legacy SHA-256-with-salt hashes.

item.title: ClickOnce COM hijacking abuse
item.description: Added a defender pattern from CrowdStrike's June 18, 2026 ClickOnce research: ClickOnce deployment can be abused for low-friction Windows execution and persistence, including a newly disclosed current-user COM hijack for the hardcoded deployment-service CLSID {20FD4E26-8E0F-4F73-A0E0-F27B8C57BE6F}. The page captures .application / .appref-ms / rundll32 dfshim.dll deployment paths, update-backed persistence, HKCU COM detection pivots, and ClickOnce incident-response guidance.

item.title: Agent localhost control-plane RCE: AutoJack PyPI pre-release caveat
item.description: Updated the AutoJack / agent localhost control-plane RCE pattern with The Hacker News' June 19, 2026 PyPI pre-release caveat: stable autogenstudio 0.4.2.2 lacks the vulnerable MCP WebSocket route, but pre-release builds 0.4.3.dev1 and 0.4.3.dev2 reportedly included the unauthenticated handler that accepted command parameters from requests. The page now distinguishes stable installs from --pre / pinned dev builds, points affected users to AutoGen main at or after commit b047730, and reinforces loopback control-plane authentication and browsing-agent isolation guidance.

item.title: @withgoogle/stitch-sdk scope squat
item.description: Added coverage for SafeDep's June 20, 2026 report on @withgoogle/stitch-sdk, a malicious npm package that impersonated Google's Stitch AI design tool by squatting the @withgoogle scope. The page captures the preinstall and CLI credential-harvesting paths, Claude Code / Git / GitHub CLI / npm / Docker credential targets, stitch-production[.]org exfiltration, and defender guidance for package blocking, endpoint triage, credential rotation, and vendor-scope governance.

item.title: Malicious infrastructure provider concentration
item.description: Added a pattern page from Hunt.io's Middle East malicious-infrastructure report: more than 1,350 active C2 servers across 98 providers in 14 countries during a February-May 2026 window, with strong concentration in a small set of telecommunications and hosting networks. The page turns the report into reusable defender guidance for ASN/provider enrichment, recurrence tracking, abuse-response context, careful telecom-vs-VPS scoping, and egress/hunting pivots around Tactical RMM, Keitaro, Mozi, Hajime, Mirai, Sliver, Cobalt Strike, and related C2 families.

item.title: Gravity SMTP CVE-2026-4020 exploitation
item.description: Added coverage for active exploitation of Gravity SMTP CVE-2026-4020, an unauthenticated WordPress plugin information-disclosure flaw that can expose a full System Report and configured outbound-mail API keys or OAuth tokens. The page captures the /wp-json/gravitysmtp/v1/tests/mock-data?page=gravitysmtp-settings pivot, affected versions through 2.1.4, the 2.1.5 security-enhancement fix, Wordfence-reported active exploitation via The Hacker News, and defender guidance for patching, log review, email-provider token rotation, and follow-on WordPress compromise triage.

item.title: Operation Endgame SocGholish disruption
item.description: Added coverage for the June 18, 2026 Operation Endgame action against SocGholish / FakeUpdates: Dutch Police, RCMP, FBI, BKA, Europol, Eurojust, and private-sector partners reported 106 servers and domains taken down, 14,971 infected WordPress sites remediated, Shadowserver notification, and WordPress owner cleanup guidance. The page focuses on legitimate-site compromise, TDS redirects, fake browser-update lures, TA569 / Evil Corp source-attributed naming, and reinfection-resistant WordPress / hosting triage.

item.title: FortiBleed Fortinet credential exposure: Unit 42 cross-service password-spray update
item.description: Updated FortiBleed coverage with Unit 42's June 19 threat brief: suspicious login attempts in customer telemetry, observed MSSQL targeting, reported Sophos targeting, a staged password-spray / configuration-theft / offline-cracking loop, and an unvalidated Exploit[.]in initial-access-broker claim. The page now tells defenders to expand review beyond Fortinet appliances to other internet-facing login services and to hunt for successful logins shortly after high-volume failure bursts.

item.title: The Gentlemen ransomware: GentleKiller EDR-killer framework update
item.description: Updated The Gentlemen ransomware page with ESET's June 18, 2026 GentleKiller analysis: Gentlemen operators maintain an affiliate EDR-killer portfolio, at least eight GentleKiller variants abuse vulnerable or malicious drivers, HexKiller / ThrottleBlood / HavocKiller are operationally integrated, shared evasion impersonates security vendors with copied metadata and icons, and newly disclosed BYOVD PoCs are adopted rapidly. The update adds defender pivots for vulnerable-driver loading, driver-blocklist enforcement, HVCI, and tamper-protection hardening.

item.title: JetBrains AI plugin API-key theft
item.description: Added coverage for StepSecurity and JetBrains reporting on 15 malicious JetBrains Marketplace AI plugins that stole OpenAI, DeepSeek, SiliconFlow, and other provider API keys from developer IDE settings. The page captures affected plugin IDs, seven banned publisher accounts, plaintext HTTP exfiltration to 39.107.60[.]51, the static X-Api-Key header, JetBrains removal and remote-disable response, key-rotation guidance, and IDE-plugin hunting pivots.

item.title: Ababil of Minab MOIS-linked recovery-destruction campaign: Hunt.io exposed-staging follow-up
item.description: Updated the Ababil of Minab recovery-destruction page with Hunt.io's June 18 exposed-staging follow-up: a Python SimpleHTTP server at 5.255.127[.]55:8020, 2,238 staged files across 545 subdirectories, about 5 GB of victim material, LA Metro database-backup confirmation, http.flask.py and .bash_history workflow artifacts, FileFiend / archive-retrieval support, and explicit handling guidance to preserve evidence without redistributing victim data.

item.title: Klue Salesforce OAuth token abuse
item.description: Added coverage for the Klue integration incident affecting connected customer SaaS environments: a compromised legacy integration credential reportedly let an attacker obtain OAuth tokens, query customer CRM data including Salesforce, and trigger Salesforce to disable the Klue Battlecards app integration. The page captures Klue, Huntress, Salesforce, and The Hacker News reporting, plus SaaS OAuth grant triage, connected-app logging, token revocation, and stale vendor-credential controls.

item.title: npm install explicit-trust controls: developer package-config drift update
item.description: Updated the npm install explicit-trust controls pattern with StepSecurity's developer-machine package-configuration guidance: internal registries, secure registries, package cooldowns, and auth policy only protect hosts actually configured to use them. The page now captures npm and Python package-manager config inventory, public-index fallback detection, endpoint cooldown enforcement, token hygiene, and drift monitoring across developer laptops and CI runners.

item.title: Agent localhost control-plane RCE
item.description: Added a pattern page for Microsoft Security Research's AutoJack case study: untrusted web content rendered by a browsing AI agent can cross the localhost boundary, reach a local MCP WebSocket control plane, and turn caller-supplied stdio server parameters into host command execution. The page captures the AutoGen Studio development-branch caveat, upstream hardening before PyPI release, and durable guidance for authenticating loopback control planes, allowlisting MCP launchers, isolating browsing agents, and hunting agent-spawned child processes.

item.title: GHOST STADIUM FIFA World Cup ticket phishing
item.description: Added coverage for Hunt.io's June 17 GHOST STADIUM FIFA World Cup 2026 ticketing phishing report: cloned FIFA ticketing portals on lookalike domains, same-origin credential and payment harvesting, reusable /fifa/ React-build and Layui pivots, suspected AS25820 / 16clouds origin hosting, favicon clustering, and a caveated Chinese-speaking operator assessment.

item.title: procwire / routecraft npm Windows dropper
item.description: Added coverage for SafeDep's June 18 report on a five-package npm campaign: procwire and routecraft execute a Windows-only preinstall dropper while bytecraft, endpointmap, and staticlayer split XOR endpoint reconstruction and payload-serving logic across helper packages. The page captures package/version pivots, files.catbox.moe staging, Microsoft-Delivery-Optimization User-Agent gating, updater-like temp executable names, Mark-of-the-Web stripping, and Windows npm-install response guidance.

item.title: Splunk Enterprise CVE-2026-20253 KEV exploitation update
item.description: Updated the Splunk Enterprise CVE-2026-20253 page after CISA added the unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Service flaw to KEV on 2026-06-18.
